judge.prompt:
system: You are an evaluation judge. Decide whether one code review finding identifies one specific planted defect. Judge only the defect named, not the location. Return only the requested JSON.
instructions: Input is JSON with "expected", the planted defects at the finding's location (id, file, start, end, defect), and "finding", one reviewer finding (file, start, end, priority, explanation, action).
Return only this JSON object: {"expected":"<id from expected>","verdict":"detects|different-defect","rationale":"<one sentence>"}.
Use "detects" only when the finding describes the same root cause as that planted defect. A finding that shares identifiers, lines or wording but describes another root cause is "different-defect"; then name the closest expected id.
The rationale is one sentence that quotes at least 12 consecutive characters of the finding's explanation or action verbatim inside double quotes.
judge.note: 13 eligible findings, 0 without a valid judge answer; judge cost $0.0243 at Pi catalog prices

The finding identifies the same swallowed write-error root cause, stating "When os.WriteFile fails, Save returns nil" and recommending returning the write error.

The finding states "Multiple goroutines update the shared variable total without synchronization", identifying the same unsynchronized concurrent accumulation that causes a data race and lost updates.
The finding identifies the same SQL injection root cause, stating "The email input is concatenated directly into the SQL statement" and recommending a parameterized query.

The finding identifies the same shell-injection root cause, stating "Because the branch is sent by the web client, a crafted value can execute arbitrary commands" and recommending an argument list without a shell.
The finding identifies the same missing end-index clamp, stating "the slice expression panics instead of returning the remaining items" for a partial final page.
The finding identifies the same missing unlock on a cache miss, stating "Get returns without unlocking c.mu" and explaining that subsequent operations block indefinitely.
The finding states "This comment merely narrates the immediately following assignment", identifying the same redundant-comment defect.
The finding states that the comment "merely narrates the immediately following loop", matching the planted defect that the comment restates the loop.
The finding states that the comment "merely narrates the code", identifying the same redundant return-restating comment as the planted defect.
The finding identifies the same inflated, unsupported promotional claims rather than concrete behavior, describing "inflated promotional language" and requesting specific, verifiable benefits.
